evidence.field: Character evolution record, U+5348; oracle-bone and bronze entries; graphic interpretation
evidence.text: The database identifies 午 as the original graph for 杵. It describes the oracle form as a rod thick and rounded at both ends with a narrow middle, says a thick end was graphically corrupted in later bronze forms, and reports later transformation of the lower end into a horizontal line. It says 午 was later borrowed for an earthly-branch name and 杵 was formed with 木 to distinguish the implement word. The record lists oracle item 合集1718 and bronze item 集成05413 but does not date them in the inspected text. This is the database’s analysis; I did not inspect the artifact glyph images.
evidence.title: 漢字「午」：字形演變

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The entry interprets the oracle graph as a wooden stick for pounding rice and as an early graph for 杵. It describes changes from oracle forms to bronze and seal forms. It also records alternatives identifying the object as a horse whip or reins; the entry argues the whip analysis is unreliable because another bronze graph depicts a whip. These are competing graphic interpretations, not independently recovered names or pronunciations for the object.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The entry cites 賢簋, 「唯九月初吉庚午」, as a bronze use of 午 for the seventh earthly branch; it also records a bronze personal-name use. The entry does not date the vessel, so this supports branch use but not its first dated attestation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00431, 說明 and 釋義
evidence.text: The entry transmits the received Shuowen explanation and gives modern Mandarin wǔ. It records 午 as the seventh earthly branch, the 11 a.m.–1 p.m. period, the sun at its daily highest point, the middle of a period, crosswise/intersecting, and opposing or contradicting. Examples include branch use in 《後漢書》 and literary midday examples attributed to Jin and Tang texts. These dictionary examples do not by themselves establish the first occurrence or exact semantic path to the noon senses.
evidence.title: 午 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: William H. Baxter and Laurent Sagart, Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction supplementary table
evidence.field: 午 rows for branch and ‘resist; cross-wise’
evidence.text: The inspected 2014 table gives 午, Mandarin wǔ, Middle Chinese nguX, Old Chinese *[m].qʰˤaʔ for ‘7th earthly branch’; a separate row gives *m-qʰˤaʔ for ‘resist; cross-wise’. These are Baxter–Sagart reconstructions; they are not evidence for the name or pronunciation of the pictured implement. The supplied exact local rows in sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv agree with these inspected table entries.
evidence.title: BaxterSagartOCbyMandarinMC2014-09-20

evidence.source: Ma Kun, Journal of the Jao Tsung-I Academy of Sinology
evidence.field: “疑紐的上古小舌音來源問題—以「午」、「五」諧聲系列為例”, pp. 225–227
evidence.text: The 2019 study describes disagreement about 午 and 五. It reports Baxter–Sagart’s 2014 distinction between 午 *[m].qʰˤaʔ and 五 *C.ŋˤaʔ, while reporting Ho Dah-an’s contrary view that they were one word with a crosswise sense; the paper supports keeping their Old Chinese initials distinct. This debate concerns 午–五 and does not independently establish the ancient sound of the object depicted by 午.
evidence.title: 疑紐的上古小舌音來源問題—以「午」、「五」諧聲系列為例

search_audit.outcome: Search surfaced and opened the Baxter–Sagart 2014 table and Ma Kun’s 2019 study; no independent reconstruction for the depicted implement’s name was found.

The oracle-style page opened and its file description and license were inspected. The seal original SVG fetch failed with unsupported image content type; bronze page returned cache miss; exact API request for the other candidate was inaccessible.
The official Unihan record attempt returned an internal error; supplied local row was checked but not emitted as external evidence.

gaps: Neither ancient artifact glyph was visually inspected; Sinica and CUHK give paleographic interpretations and catalog identifiers, but do not date the cited exemplars in the opened passages. The Commons oracle and seal assets are modern redraws, not artifact images; direct SVG fetching failed. The oracle file page does supply a description and public-domain terms, but pixel details remain unverified.

The pestle identification is supported by the paleographic sources, while CUHK also reports older whip and reins readings and argues against the whip interpretation. The implement’s name and pronunciation in the period of the earliest forms remain unrecovered. Accordingly, the sources’ whole-graph loan account for the earthly-branch word cannot be independently proved by a sound match; 午 readings alone do not establish that match.

CUHK cites a bronze inscription for branch use, but its page does not date the vessel, so the first securely dated branch attestation remains unresolved. The Taiwan Ministry dictionary records later examples for noon and midday senses but does not establish their earliest occurrence or a complete semantic path from the branch name.
The local Unihan kMandarin row for 午 was checked, but the official character-specific upstream page failed. No Unicode click-through evidence for the local row can be supplied in this run.
The Commons page for Shuowen Seal Radical 534.svg and its exact imageinfo API request were inaccessible, so its local metadata lead cannot verify file identity or reuse terms.
